title: Tensor sections describe change of topology for arbitrary scheme modules
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with Zariski site $T_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ of open subschemes [def-sc-zariski-site] and small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. On the latter put $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}(u:V\to T)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. The inclusion of open subschemes induces a morphism of ringed sites [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] $\epsilon_T:(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}})\to(T_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_T)$ whose module direct image is restriction: $(\epsilon_{T,*}G)(W)=G(W\hookrightarrow T)$ for each open $W\subseteq T$. For every sheaf $M$ of $\mathcal O_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], without any quasi-coherence hypothesis, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\epsilon_T^{-1}\mathcal O_T}\epsilon_T^{-1}M\ \simeq\ \big(u:V\to T\longmapsto\Gamma(V,u^*M)\big)^{\#}.$$
Here tensor product is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $u^*M$ is scheme module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and $\#$ is module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The presheaf restrictions are pullback of sections followed by the canonical composition isomorphisms, and its action on a module morphism $h$ is $\Gamma(V,u^*h)$.

proof.text: Put $j:T_{\mathrm{Zar}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for inclusion. The site morphism $\epsilon_T$ and the formula $\epsilon_*G(W)=G(W\hookrightarrow T)$ are precisely [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites]. The underlying additive presheaf of $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ is the sheaf of [def-sc-etale-additive-structure-restriction], after removing its harmless universe lift. Thus compatible functions glue uniquely; their sums, products, zero and unit glue because restriction is a ring map. This proves the ring-sheaf assertion. On an open $W$, $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)=\mathcal O_T(W)$, compatibly with restriction and ring operations. Hence $\mathcal O_T\to\epsilon_*\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ is the identity under these identifications. Its adjoint is the structural map $\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$, giving the claimed ringed morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Its induced module pushforward is the displayed restriction with its ordinary scalar action.

proof.text: For any $M$, put $P_M(u:V\to T)=\Gamma(V,u^*M)$. Use the unit-normalized composition isomorphisms and pullback of sections from [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]. That statement applies to every module: its three clauses prove semilinearity, identities, and composition for the restrictions. Thus $P_M$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules. The maps $P_h(V)=\Gamma(V,u^*h)$ commute with restrictions by [lem-sc-etale-tensor-sections-map-naturality]. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $L(M)=P_M^\#$ is a functor, and maps $L(M)\to G$ are uniquely the module-presheaf maps $P_M\to G$.

source.place: Tag 070S, lemma-compare-sites (2), omitted proof supplied using Tag 0096, sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules

proof.text: Fix an etale module sheaf $G$. For every $u:V\to T$, define an ordinary Zariski module sheaf $G_u$ on $V$ by $G_u(A)=G(A\hookrightarrow V\xrightarrow{u}T)$ for each open $A\subseteq V$. Open covers are etale covers, so the sheaf axiom for $G$ gives exactly the Zariski sheaf axiom for $G_u$; its scalars are $\mathcal O_V(A)$. For any $T$-map $a:V'\to V$, restrictions of $G$ give a module map $r_a:G_u\to a_*G_{u'}$, where $u'=ua$: on $A$ this is $G(A)\to G(a^{-1}A)$ and semilinearity is over $a^\sharp$. Functoriality of these maps is simply functoriality of restrictions. For $u=\mathrm{id}_T$, $G_u=\epsilon_*G$.

source.place: Tag 070S, lemma-compare-sites (2), omitted proof supplied using Tag 0096, sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules

proof.text: An $\mathcal O_T$-linear map $\beta:M\to\epsilon_*G$ determines a module map $b_u:M\to u_*G_u$ as follows. For an open $W\subseteq T$, set $V_W=u^{-1}W$, an open of $V$ and an etale object over $T$. Send $m\in M(W)$ to the restriction of $\beta_W(m)\in G(W\hookrightarrow T)$ along the $T$-map $V_W\to W$. This is linear over $\mathcal O_T(W)$ acting through $u^\sharp$, and commutes with restrictions by the presheaf laws. The scheme module adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] therefore gives a unique $\mathcal O_V$-linear map $a_u:u^*M\to G_u$ with $u_*a_u\circ\eta^u_M=b_u$. Define $\theta_u:P_M(u)\to G(u)$ by evaluating $a_u$ on the whole $V$.

source.place: Tag 070S, lemma-compare-sites (2), omitted proof supplied using Tag 0096, sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules

proof.text: These $\theta_u$ form a presheaf map. Indeed, for $a:V'\to V$ over $T$, transpose $r_a:G_u\to a_*G_{u'}$ to $\bar r_a:a^*G_u\to G_{u'}$ using [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Compare $a_{u'}$ with $\bar r_a\circ a^*(a_u)\circ c_{a,u}^{-1}$ as maps $u'^*M\to G_{u'}$. By the composite-unit normalization in [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial], their transposes are maps $M\to u'_*G_{u'}$. On each open $W\subseteq T$, the first transpose sends $m$ to $\beta_W(m)$ restricted along $V'_W\to W$; the second restricts it first along $V_W\to W$ and then $V'_W\to V_W$. They agree by composition of restrictions. The adjunction bijection makes the two original maps equal. Evaluating at $V'$ gives $\theta_{u'}\rho_a=G(a)\theta_u$, exactly the required naturality. The construction is also natural in $M$ and $G$, since precomposition or postcomposition commutes with $b_u$ and with the adjunction bijection.

source.place: Tag 070S, lemma-compare-sites (2), omitted proof supplied using Tag 0096, sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules

proof.text: Conversely, a module-presheaf map $\theta:P_M\to G$ restricts to a module map $\beta:M\to\epsilon_*G$ on open subschemes: for $i_W:W\hookrightarrow T$, identify $i_W^*M$ with $M|_W$ by the unit-compatible isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], and apply $\theta_{i_W}$ on global sections. The resulting maps commute with open restriction: [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial] gives the normalized restriction on $P_M$, and the open comparison preserves the adjunction units, hence these are exactly the ordinary restrictions of $M$. They are $\mathcal O_T(W)$-linear since both the open comparison and $\theta_{i_W}$ are linear. If one starts with $\beta$ as in step 4, the resulting $\beta$ is the original one: at $i_W$, its adjoint map on the open $W$ is $\beta|_W$ under that same unit-compatible comparison.

source.place: Tag 070S, lemma-compare-sites (2), omitted proof supplied using Tag 0096, sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules

proof.text:
To check the other inverse, start with $\theta$ and its $\beta$ from step 6. For each $u:V\to T$, the components of $\theta$ on all open subschemes $A\subseteq V$ assemble to a Zariski module map $a_u^\theta:u^*M\to G_u$. Here identify $(u^*M)|_A$ with $(u|_A)^*M$ using the open comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] and the normalized composition of [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]; under these identifications the restrictions are those of $u^*M$. For $m\in M(W)$, its image by the unit in $\Gamma(V_W,u^*M)$ is the normalized restriction of the section corresponding to $m$ in $P_M(i_W)$. This equality is precisely composition of the open unit with the $V_W\to W$ unit, as in the normalization equation of [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]. Naturality of $\theta$ along $V_W\to W$ gives
$$a_u^\theta(\eta^u_M(m))=\beta_W(m)|_{V_W}=b_u(m).$$
The bijection of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] now implies $a_u^\theta=a_u$. On global sections this says that step 4 recovers $\theta_u$ for every $u$. Thus both inverse identities have been proved on all objects, without any hypothesis about quasi-coherence or any claim about global tensor generators.

source.place: Tag 070S, lemma-compare-sites (2), omitted proof supplied using Tag 0096, sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules

proof.text: Steps 4-7 give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(P_M,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,\epsilon_*G)$. Compose with the module-sheafification bijection of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] to obtain $L\dashv\epsilon_*$. On the other hand [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], applied to the ringed morphism in step 1, makes $Q(M)=\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal O_T}\epsilon^{-1}M$ left adjoint to this same module direct image. Both adjunctions apply to all module sheaves. The unique unit-compatible comparison between these two left adjoints is a natural isomorphism $Q\simeq L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with the identity isomorphism on their common right adjoint. This is the asserted canonical isomorphism. By step 2 its right side has exactly the specified restrictions and action $h\mapsto\Gamma(V,u^*h)$.
